log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Provide a reference for validating customer onboarding fields, with a pattern, valid example, and user-facing error message for each field.","tasks":["Find a field and read its validation rule, example, and error message across the row.","Compare patterns and constraints across fields when implementing or checking validation.","Read error messages and examples to understand the expected input."],"relations":["Each row connects one field identifier to its regex, a valid value, and the message shown when validation fails.","The example and error message explain the same constraints expressed more compactly by the regex."],"roles":["The first column identifies rows; the remaining columns contain the pattern, example, and error message for each field.","The header labels each column; the seven body rows have equal structural importance."],"keep_whole":["Field identifiers, regex tokens and syntax, example values, numbers, and meaningful units such as YYYY-MM-DD where space permits.","The long email regex is wider than a phone viewport even before the other columns are included."],"may_wrap":["Error messages can wrap at natural word boundaries.","Patterns and long examples may need to wrap at available break points in compact layouts, with some identifiers or tokens splitting in a viewport-fitting layout."],"same_scale":["All field identifiers share one column scale; examples and error messages should each remain consistent within their own columns.","Pattern and prose columns need different widths because their content and reading tasks differ."],"h_vs_v":"Fitting all four columns on a phone makes every column narrower than its longest unbreakable content and produces extensive splitting and tall rows. Scrolling preserves identifiers and gives examples and messages usable reading widths, at the cost of moving horizontally to connect information across each row."},"designs":[{"widths":[85,90,88,96],"strategy":"Fit the viewport with a compact four-column grid, accepting extensive splitting and tall rows to keep all column relationships visible at once."},{"widths":[147,180,188,260],"strategy":"Use a moderately scrolling reference layout that keeps field identifiers and measured unbreakable examples whole while giving messages room to wrap naturally."},{"widths":[147,420,285,360],"strategy":"Use a wide implementation-oriented layout that gives patterns substantial space and keeps examples on one line, trading more horizontal travel for shorter rows and easier inspection of rules."}]}
